pr.title: Type-check the hooks module in the local gate
pr.head: 30fc6a257efe1ea95d5e6e4d2a518b4742e4168f

summary: Projector ships a Claude Code hooks module in hooks/: TypeScript that draws Projector's band above the prompt and reads the inbox. Claude Code compiles and runs it, but the validation gate never type-checked it. claude plugin validate . and claude plugin test . both pass code that tsc rejects, which is how the type error that #287 fixed reached main.
This change adds hooks/typecheck.sh to the local gate. The script runs the TypeScript compiler that site/ already installs, through a new root tsconfig.json that covers only hooks/.

The compiler needs Claude Code's own declarations: the claude-code module, its claude-code/testing kit, and the inputs of the built-in tools. Claude Code writes them to .claude-plugin/types/ when an interactive session loads a checkout with claude --plugin-dir ., and nothing else provides them. So the check runs only in the local gate, and the Check workflow in CI does not run it. A linked worktree that has no declarations or no tsc of its own borrows the main checkout's. When neither checkout has them, the step fails with a setup message.

cards.title: Set up a checkout once
cards.html:
1. Run npm ci in site/, which installs tsc.
  2. Start claude --plugin-dir . from the repository root and quit at the prompt. Claude Code writes the declarations to .claude-plugin/types/, which Git ignores.
  3. Run hooks/typecheck.sh. Repeat step 2 after you update Claude Code.

A linked worktree can skip steps 1 and 2 when the main checkout has done them.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• Three Projector reviews, of c38d3b1, 2a5af53, and 30fc6a2, found each head clean, with no finding threads.
  • 2a5af53 added the borrowed declarations. 30fc6a2 added the borrowed tsc and reworded the claim that the declarations depend only on the Claude Code version, which the second review suggested. Both reviews tested the borrows in a throwaway clone with a linked worktree.
  • No review could get declarations that Claude Code wrote. Each ran the check against a copy rebuilt from the declarations Claude Code 2.1.296 bundles with its plugin-authoring skill.

groups.title: The type check and its configuration
groups.kicker: A gate script, the root tsconfig it compiles with, and the ignore rule for the declarations
intro: hooks/typecheck.sh first looks for tsc in site/. When this checkout has none, the script borrows the main checkout's, the first entry git worktree list prints. When this checkout has the declarations, the script runs tsc -p . from the repository root. When it has none, the script borrows them from the main checkout. To do that, it writes a tsconfig.json to a temporary directory that extends the main checkout's declarations and includes this worktree's hooks/, and deletes the directory on exit. The script prints a using line for each borrow. It exits 1 with a setup instruction when neither checkout has the compiler or the declarations, and otherwise exits with the compiler's status, 2 on a type error.

The root tsconfig.json extends the tsconfig.json Claude Code writes in .claude-plugin/types/. That file carries the compiler options a hooks module needs, such as JSX compiled to h, and makes the folder the type root. The root file only narrows include to hooks. It sits at the root because Claude Code writes its own root tsconfig.json into a plugin that has none, and a committed one stops that untracked file from appearing.

checks.text: The check catches the errors it exists for. With declarations rebuilt from Claude Code 2.1.296's bundled copy, the head exits 0. A deliberate error in hooks/parse.ts exits 2 with TS2322, and the hooks/ tree from 7e0a5e0 exits 2 with the one hooks/register.tsx(282,60) error that #287 fixed.

The root tsconfig.json does not change how Claude Code loads the plugin. With .claude-plugin/types/ removed, as in an installed copy, claude plugin test . passes all 78 tests. A root tsconfig.json with a bogus jsxFactory also passes them, so the engine does not read the file at load time.

files.note: The gate step: finds tsc and the declarations in this checkout or, failing that, the main checkout, then type-checks hooks/.

checks.text: A worktree with no tsc borrows the main checkout's and still checks its own files. In a throwaway clone with a linked worktree, an error added to the worktree's hooks/parse.ts exits 2 with the borrowed tsc. With no tsc in either checkout, the script exits 1 with this message, which the review's scratch worktree reproduced.

The script tests only that a tsconfig.json exists in .claude-plugin/types/. Declarations written by an older Claude Code pass this test, which is why the documentation says to start a session again after an update.
With no declarations in either checkout, the script exits 1 with this message, after any using line for tsc.

The declaration borrow checks the right code. In the throwaway clone, borrowing both tsc and the declarations exits 0, and an error added to the worktree's hooks/parse.ts exits 2, so the status survives the EXIT trap. The temporary directory is gone after both runs. An earlier review also showed that an error only in the main checkout passes, and that a worktree path with a space and a double quote works.

files.note: Extends Claude Code's generated tsconfig.json and limits the program to hooks/.

checks.text: site/ keeps its own tsconfig.json, so npm run check in site/ still passes with this file at the root.

files.note: Ignores .claude-plugin/types/, which Claude Code writes into the checkout.

groups.title: Gate documentation
groups.kicker: Where contributors learn about the new step and its one-time setup
intro: Three documents list the gate, and each now lists hooks/typecheck.sh and says that a linked worktree borrows the main checkout's tsc and declarations when it has none. AGENTS.md is the file agents follow, and CLAUDE.md is a symlink to it. docs/develop.md turns the old one-line npm ci reminder into two setup steps. docs/plugins.md adds the step to the checks a plugin author runs before publishing.

files.note: Adds the step to the gate and explains why CI cannot run it.
Two setup steps before the gate, and a note that the Check workflow cannot type-check hooks/.

checks.text: The claim that Projector loads only with gh-stack installed matches dependencies in .claude-plugin/plugin.json, and the plugins.md#install-for-claude-code anchor resolves.
